steps.body: A full graph-read answers four questions in order: **where is it increasing/decreasing**, **where are the extrema**, **what are the domain and range**, and **what story do the numbers tell** (if the axes carry units). One pass, left to right, collecting all four.
Range from behavior: the downward parabola.

widget.prompt: y = −(x − 2)² + 9 has absolute maximum value 9 and falls forever on both sides. What is the LARGEST number in its range?

commonErrors.feedback: 2 is the input of the vertex. The range collects OUTPUTS, and the largest output is the maximum value, 9.
5 is just one output (at x = 0 or 4). The range tops out at the vertex height, 9.

steps.body: Range follows from extrema and end behavior: this parabola's outputs fill **(−∞, 9]** — everything up to and including the summit. The cubic x³ − 3x, despite its local peak and valley, has range **all reals**: its arms escape both upward and downward past every bound.

explanationVariants: y = |x − 3| + 1 has floor value 1 and climbs forever both ways: range [1, ∞).
Outputs are 1 + (a nonnegative number), so exactly the values ≥ 1 occur.

widget.prompt: What is the range of y = |x − 3| + 1?

commonBuilds.feedback: 3 is the corner's INPUT. Range is about outputs, which start at the floor VALUE 1: [1, ∞).
The outputs never dip below 1: |x − 3| is at least 0 and the +1 lifts everything, so the range is [1, ∞), not all reals.

widget.missFeedback: Floor of 1 at the corner, unbounded above: the range is [1, ∞).
widget.successFeedback: Right — floor 1 at the corner, unbounded above.

steps.body: Local extrema don't cap a range.
explanationVariants: The cubic's arms run down-left and up-right past every bound, so every real number is an output despite the bumps at ±1.
f(−10) = −970 and f(10) = 970 — the wiggle between −2 and 2 never limits the reachable outputs.

widget.prompt: y = x³ − 3x has a local max value 2 and a local min value −2. What is its range?

options.label: All real numbers
options.feedback: Yes — the arms escape both ways, so LOCAL extrema place no cap on the range.
Those are the heights of the two LOCAL bumps, not global fences: f(3) = 18 is already outside [−2, 2].
The graph spends plenty of time below 2 (f(0) = 0, f(1) = −2) and even runs to −∞ leftward. Range: all reals.

explanationVariants: Increasing then decreasing with a single peak: the ball rises, tops out, and falls — the peak's y is the greatest height.
The vertex is the moment the climb becomes a fall; its output is the maximum height reached.

widget.prompt: H(t) graphs a ball's height over time: increasing on (0, 2), decreasing on (2, 4), maximum point (2, 20). What does (2, 20) mean?

options.label: At 2 seconds the ball reaches its greatest height, 20 meters
options.feedback: Exactly — x is WHEN (2 s), y is the peak height (20 m).

options.label: The ball travels 20 meters in each of the first 2 seconds
options.feedback: That would be a RATE (m/s). The point (2, 20) is a position on the graph: time 2 s, height 20 m.

options.label: The ball lands at time 20
options.feedback: Coordinates reversed — 2 is the time, 20 the height. Landing is where H returns to 0, at t = 4.

explanationVariants: Increasing (−∞, 2); absolute max value 9 at x = 2; range (−∞, 9]; and g(5) = −(3)² + 9 = 0 — the graph crosses the axis at x = 5.
Everything hangs off the vertex (2, 9): climb to it, fall after, outputs capped at 9, and the fall passes height 0 at x = 5 since g(5) = 0.
hints: Evaluate g(5) directly: substitute x = 5 into −(x − 2)² + 9.
−9 + 9 = 0 — the curve touches the x-axis there.

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is the maximum value at the VERTEX x = 2. At x = 5: −(3)² + 9 = −9 + 9 = 0.
You may have ADDED (5−2)² instead of subtracting: g(5) = −(3)² + 9 = 0, not 9 + 9.
−(3)² = −9 is only the first term — remember the +9: total 0.

takeaways: Read behavior, extrema, domain/range, and story together.
Range comes from extrema PLUS end behavior — local bumps don't cap it.
With units, every point is a sentence: x is when/where, y is how much.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: symmetry — functions that mirror themselves — and graphs built from pieces.

concept.body: Range = the outputs actually reached. Find the extreme VALUES, then ask where the arms go: capped side closed, escaping side infinite.

explanationVariants: y = x² has floor 0 and opens upward forever: range [0, ∞).
Squares produce exactly the nonnegative numbers.

widget.prompt: What is the range of y = x²?

options.feedback: Right — floor 0 at the vertex, unbounded above.
x² is never negative — outputs start at 0. Range [0, ∞).
